hints.title: Array Values as Directed Pointers
hints.text: Treat the array as a directed functional graph where an edge exists from index i to value nums[i].

hints.title: Floyd Cycle Detection Analogy
hints.text: Because values lie between one and n with n plus one elements, a cycle must exist. The entrance to the cycle is the duplicate value.

hints.title: Two Pointers Intersection and Cycle Entry
hints.text: Advance slow by one step and fast by two steps until they meet. Reset slow to nums[0], then advance both by one step until they meet again. That meeting value is the duplicate.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: size of array nums minus 1
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Modifying the array violates read-only constraints, and tracking seen numbers violates O(1) space constraints.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Floyd cycle detection finds the cycle entry in linear time with zero array modifications and O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should clearly explain the reduction to linked list cycle detection and why fast and slow pointers meet at the cycle entrance.
